system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| ID | Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** | General liability cap | 20% of price: **AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m** general Warranty cap. | **Reject and counter at AUD 6m** — the 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval for this draft, which has not been given. |
| **SPA-N-002** | De minimis & basket | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Replace both thresholds and make the basket tipping** — Seller’s proposal materially suppresses otherwise valid claims. |
| **SPA-N-003** | General claims time limit | General Claims notified within 18 months; limitations potentially apply to all Claims. | **24 months after Completion** for general Warranty Claims only. | **Counter at 24 months and confine it to general Warranty Claims** — 18 months is an unauthorised fallback and must not override separate claim regimes. |
| **SPA-N-004** | Fundamental/Title regime | Same caps and time limits as general warranties. | Separate regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, outside general de minimis, basket and knowledge bars. | **Reject Seller’s proposed consolidation** — ownership, authority and title risk should not be limited to AUD 4.8m or 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-005** | Fraud carve-out | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no adequate express carve-out. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all** caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert an overriding express carve-out** — this protection is mandatory under the playbook and cannot be waived. |
| **SPA-N-006** | Disclosure scope | General disclosure of the whole data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed** with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope. | **Delete deemed/general disclosure** — a data-room dump or theoretically searchable record should not qualify warranties. |
| **SPA-N-007** | Buyer knowledge qualifier | No Claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion; no constructive, adviser-imputed or “discoverable” knowledge, and no knowledge bar for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete clause 8.3 or narrow it substantially** — it improperly shifts diligence and disclosure risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008** | Bluefen consent | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. | Effective consent **and evidence that all associated conditions are satisfied before Completion**. | **Strengthen the CP and prohibit deemed satisfaction on delivery alone** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and reasonable endeavours do not secure the required outcome. |
| **SPA-N-009** | Riverlark facility | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases of all security at Completion. | **Require payout and releases through the Completion funds flow** — a post-Completion release is unacceptable without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval, neither of which exists. |
| **SPA-N-010** | Employee bonuses | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are treated as Seller’s matter but omitted from the funds flow; on-costs are unaddressed. | Express line item or other clear Seller funding for **AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs**. | **Add them expressly to the Completion mechanics** — omission risks Buyer or the Company economically bearing Seller-triggered liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-011** | Ironquay IP indemnity | Narrow indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; relies on an unverified AUD 180,000 open amount. | Broader protection for losses and claims arising from failure to obtain/own/use the relevant Ironquay IP, while preserving the SOW3 payment-and-assignment cure. | **Broaden the indemnity and require payment/assignment evidence** — neither non-payment nor valid transfer is independently established. |
| **SPA-N-012** | Export/privacy incident | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; no confirmed access, breach, notification duty or loss. | Log preservation, prompt investigation, Buyer updates, access/scope assessment and compliance/remediation obligations without prejudging outcome. | **Add investigation and information covenants, preserving Buyer’s rights** — the current evidence supports neither minimisation nor an assumed breach, notification obligation or numeric claim. |
| **SPA-N-013** | Sandbar renewals | Three AUD 110,000 renewals, AUD 330,000 total, characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Determine timing, accrual, termination rights, scope and whether they are unavoidable; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction. | **Continue diligence before assigning treatment** — the materials do not establish that the renewals are ordinary-course, accrued, unavoidable or terminable. |
| **SPA-N-014** | Category separation | Seller proposes broadly applying limitations to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities, without hidden general-regime overrides. | **Rewrite the limitation architecture with express category-specific rules** — “all Claims” wording could unintentionally erode negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015** | Title verification | Relies on the DD-012 internal Company share register as evidence of 100% ownership. | Independent evidence of ownership, authority, valid issue and absence/release of encumbrances, alongside the register. | **Require independent title and encumbrance verification** — DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not conclusive independent proof. |
| **SPA-N-016** | Tax/IP open terms | Seller says Tax and IP positions are settled under the general regime. | Treat Tax and IP as **open**, negotiate their substantive warranties, indemnities, caps and periods separately, with no assumption of unlimited liability. | **Reject any assertion that these terms are settled** — Seller’s statement is not Buyer authority and the playbook records both categories as unresolved. |
=== END ADVICE ===
